class.name: Paladin
class.text: A paladin keeps one seal, one aura and one blessing on each friend, and every one of them lasts a set time (a seal 30 seconds, a blessing 5 minutes). Mana runs the class. Retribution fights with a seal and Judgement, Holy heals, Protection holds. Every line below presses a button.

card.caresAbout: the seal on you, the Judgement that spends it, the aura and blessing you chose, and the mana to do it again
card.vocabulary: seal, judge, aura, blessing, swing, cooldown, mana
card.soundsLike: calm and exact, one thing at a time, a clause longer than the Warrior. A paladin line says what is on you before it says what to press
card.neverSays: rage, stance, anything about the Light, faith, justice as an idea or a crusade (the spells have those words and the line uses them as names only)
card.test: could the line be followed by someone who has never heard of the Light?

advice.say: Take it if you level alone. A damage paladin works with a seal and Judgement and heals between pulls with Holy Light, so it needs no group. The price: no taunt and no way to heal in a fight, so in a dungeon you will want a tank and a healer beside you.
Take it if you will mostly play in a group, because a paladin who heals is always wanted there. The price: a Holy paladin kills slowly alone, so levelling takes longer.

Take it if you will hold monsters for a group. The price: the book has no taunt, so a monster that goes for someone else stays on them until you hit it again. Protection also levels slowly alone and has no threat on a pack until Consecration, which this path takes at 51.

overview.who: You fight in melee with a seal on you and heal yourself between pulls. It is slow work and hard to kill, and it runs on mana, not rage.
overview.good: Staying alive while you hit things. A group wants your auras and blessings, and you can always heal yourself when the fight is over.
overview.bad: Speed. You kill one monster at a time and wait for mana between pulls. A pack of three is a problem you solve with patience.
overview.resource: Mana. Seals, Judgement and heals spend it, and a swing costs none. When the bar is empty, keep swinging and sit down afterwards.
overview.levelling: Seal on, Judgement when it is ready, swing the rest of the time. Heal when the fight is over and drink when the bar is low. Aura and blessing go on before the first pull and stay on.
overview.ten: You get your first talent point. Pick damage, tank or heal and Primer shows the build and your first three picks. A respec costs gold, so choose what you will do most.

builds.name: Retribution
builds.intro: Retribution fights in melee with one big weapon and a seal that adds to every swing. It is the paladin that kills alone. The rest of the page is about which seal, and when to spend it with Judgement.
builds.pathNote: (31 points or more in Retribution for Repentance. The rest are Holy, and Protection on the Holy-first road.)
builds.split: the first 20 points. One road takes Retribution at once, for damage. The other takes 10 Holy points first, for mana and heals a hit does not spoil, and has no Seal of Command until level 30. Both end with about 30 points in Retribution. Neither is wrong.
builds.dry: Most of this page waits on Judgement. If it is not ready, hit the monster.

path.why: Judgement and your seals cost less mana, and mana is what stops a paladin.
Judgement comes back sooner, so you press it more often.
More of the attacks on you are parried.
You run faster, and the points cost you nothing you needed.
Your seal if your weapon is slow: each swing may add Holy damage. It is a talent, not a trainer spell.
More critical hits, and Vengeance needs all five.
Back to Deflection while the next row opens.
An aura that makes your party's Holy damage hit harder. One point, for a group.
More damage with a two-handed weapon, which is the reason for the weapon.
Blessing of Might gives a little more attack power. A spare point until the next row opens.
After a critical hit you deal more Physical and Holy damage for a few seconds.
A stun for a humanoid that heals itself. It is the last talent of the tree.
More Strength. The Holy block is where the last points go.
Seal of Righteousness and its Judgement do more damage.
The last point of Improved Seal of Righteousness.
Holy damage on the ground beneath you, for packs. It costs a lot of mana.
Holy Light and Flash of Light heal for more.
The rest of Improved Blessing of Might.
Lay on Hands comes back much sooner. The last two points are a matter of taste.

builds.line: One big weapon, a seal and Judgement. It kills alone, and most players level this way.

path.why: More Intellect, so more mana. This road starts with the mana.
A hit is less likely to spoil a heal, which is why this road is the safe one.
Blessing of Might gives more attack power, and you wear it every fight.
More of the attacks on you are parried.
Seal of Command arrives here, ten levels after the other road.
You run faster, and the points open the next row.
More critical hits.
The aura that hurts monsters hitting you hurts them more.
The rest of Conviction, which Vengeance needs.
More damage with a two-handed weapon.
A small mana discount, two of its five points.
After a critical hit you deal more Physical and Holy damage for a few seconds.
You block more after being critically hit. The armour talents come last on this road.
More chance to hit with melee weapons.
Blessing of Protection comes back sooner, and Blessing of Freedom lasts longer.
The last point is yours to place. Repentance takes the tree's deepest talent.

hardcore: Judgement, seal, swing. Do not pull five monsters at once without your cooldowns ready.
Divine Shield is your escape from level 34. When a fight has gone wrong, press it, then heal or walk away.
Keep a shield in your bags and put it on when you run from a hard hitter.
Never run out of mana in a fight. Without it you have no heal and no Judgement.

builds.roadReason: Most guides take this road. The other road trades Seal of Command until level 30 and early damage for mana and heals a hit does not spoil.
builds.hardcoreReason: On a Hardcore realm this is the safer road. The other road trades that safety for damage.

builds.name: Holy
builds.intro: Holy keeps people alive. The page cannot give a fixed order, because a healer's job is to answer whoever is losing health. It gives what each button is for, and when.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Holy for Holy Shock, then 20 in Protection).
builds.split: the last 20 points. A second road puts them in Retribution (Benediction, Improved Judgement, Conviction) for a healer who also fights alone. Your seals cost less and Judgement comes back sooner, and you give up the aura and the armour. This page takes Protection for the group.

path.why: 10% more Intellect, so more mana and more heals.
A heal keeps casting when you are hit (70% of the time), so you can heal mid-pull.
12% more from Holy Light and Flash of Light.
The cooldown drops from 1 hour to 40 minutes, and the target gets 30% more armour for 2 minutes. It opens the row for Illumination.
After a critical heal you get back the mana the spell cost.
Your next heal is a guaranteed critical, every 2 minutes. Use it on the big heal.
Blessing of Wisdom is 20% stronger.
10% more chance to resist fear and disorient. You take it to reach the next row.
5% more critical chance on Holy spells.
An instant heal on a friend, or damage on an enemy, every 30 seconds.
Devotion Aura gives 25% more armour to the group.
10% more armour from your gear.
10 more Defense skill, so fewer hits land.
The aura adds 15% to its effect, and the group resists silence and interrupt 15% more.
Blessing of Protection comes back 2 minutes sooner.

stages.opening: Devotion Aura on, Blessing of Might, Seal of Righteousness, then hit. Judgement when it is ready, the seal again after it, Holy Light once the fight is over.

rows.say: Put it on first. You and your party within 30 yards take less damage from every hit, until you change it.
rows.name: Devotion Aura

rows.say: Press it at the start of every pull. It lasts 30 seconds and adds Holy damage to each swing, and a slower weapon gets more out of it.
rows.name: Seal of Righteousness

rows.say: Whenever it is ready, every 10 seconds. It sets off the seal you wear, so put the seal back on after it.
rows.name: Judgement

rows.say: Before the first pull and again when it ends. It adds attack power for 5 minutes, so it pays back over many fights.
rows.name: Blessing of Might

rows.say: Heal when nothing is hitting you. The cast takes 2.5 seconds and a hit can ruin it, so it belongs after the pull.
rows.name: Holy Light

rows.say: You swing 40% faster but each hit is weaker. Stay on Seal of Righteousness with a slow weapon, since the slower the weapon the more it adds.
rows.name: Seal of the Crusader

rows.say: You take nothing for 6 seconds but cannot attack, and it takes 5 minutes to come back. Keep it for the fight that would otherwise kill you.
rows.name: Divine Protection

rows.say: A 3 second stun on a 1 minute cooldown. Press it to stop a monster running, or to buy the 2.5 seconds a Holy Light needs.
rows.name: Hammer of Justice

rows.say: Removes 1 disease and 1 poison. Press it when a monster's sting is the thing wearing you down.
rows.name: Purify

stages.about: A group, or one hurt friend. The page is a list of what each button is for.

rows.say: The big heal. The cast takes 2.5 seconds, so use it only when the target will live that long.
rows.name: Holy Light

rows.say: On yourself and on the other casters. It gives 10 mana every 5 seconds for 5 minutes.
rows.name: Blessing of Wisdom

rows.say: Keep it on. The group within 30 yards gets more armour, and it lasts until you change it.
rows.name: Devotion Aura

rows.say: 6 seconds in which no physical attack reaches them, but they cannot fight either. 5 minutes to come back.
rows.name: Blessing of Protection

rows.say: Removes one of each. Press it when it is the thing hurting someone.
rows.name: Purify

rows.say: Heals them for your full health and empties your mana. It takes 1 hour to come back, so save it for the moment.
rows.name: Lay on Hands

rows.say: A 1.5 second heal at a fraction of Holy Light's mana. Use it for most healing, and save Holy Light for the big hits.
rows.name: Flash of Light

rows.say: The 2.5 second cast. Save it for the moment the tank is nearly gone, because the cast is long.
rows.name: Holy Light

rows.say: Your next heal is a critical. Use it on a Holy Light for the biggest heal you will get.
rows.name: Divine Favor

rows.say: 35% chance to ignore interrupts, for all in 30 yards. Swap Devotion Aura for it when casters get hit.
rows.name: Concentration Aura

rows.say: Your swing may return 50 mana, but a healer who swings is not healing. Use it only when standing idle.
rows.name: Seal of Wisdom

rows.say: On the casters, because mana is what runs out.
rows.name: Blessing of Wisdom

rows.say: 10 seconds with no slowing or rooting. The cooldown is 20 seconds, so use it when someone is stuck.
rows.name: Blessing of Freedom

rows.say: Brings them back with a little health and mana. Cannot be cast in combat.
rows.name: Redemption

rows.say: An instant heal on a 30 second cooldown. Use it when a hole is too sudden for a cast.
rows.name: Holy Shock

rows.say: The main heal, because it costs little and casts in 1.5 seconds.
rows.name: Flash of Light

rows.say: For the tank's worst moments. Cast Divine Favor first, so this heal is a critical.
rows.name: Holy Light

rows.say: Removes one of each. Use it before the next heal if the effect is the damage.
rows.name: Cleanse

rows.say: One blessing for every healer or caster of a class in the group. It saves buffing each player one by one.
rows.name: Greater Blessing of Wisdom

rows.say: Gives a friend 3 minutes of nothing hurting them, and it costs you your life. It takes 1 hour.
rows.name: Divine Intervention

builds.line: Heals the group. It levels slowly alone, and a dungeon wants it.

builds.name: Protection
builds.intro: Protection holds monsters on you and stays up. Threat is the list a monster keeps of who to hit next. The book has no taunt, so Righteous Fury, your seal and Holy Shield are what keep a monster looking at you.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Protection for Holy Shield, then 20 in Holy).
builds.split: the last 20 points. A second road puts them in Retribution (Benediction, Deflection, Conviction, Improved Judgement, Vindication) for more parry and more critical hits. This page takes Holy because Consecration is the only way a paladin holds a pack, and the price is parry and critical chance.
builds.dry: A monster still on you after 20 seconds means the job is working.

path.why: After a critical hit on you, 30% more block for 10 seconds or 5 blocks. It also opens Shield Specialization.
10% more armour from your gear.
Righteous Fury gives 50% more threat, which is your whole job.
10 more Defense skill, so fewer hits land and fewer are critical.
3% more chance to hit, so Judgement and your seals land more.
Less damage from every hit taken, and a block hurts the attacker. It opens Holy Shield.
Your shield absorbs 30% more.
10% more damage with a one-hander, which is threat.
30% more block for 10 seconds and Holy damage for every block.
10% more Intellect, which is mana for the next pull.
15% more damage from Seal of Righteousness and its Judgement, which is threat.
Holy damage on the ground around you for 8 seconds. This is your first area threat.
12% more from Holy Light and Flash of Light.
A heal keeps casting when you are hit (70% of the time), so you can heal mid-pull.
The last point. Any talent you can reach would do as well.
